match.reason: The bank point covers the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917, not how peasants, sans-culottes and women were changed by the French Revolution, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: The revolution and ordinary people
card: most people in France worked the land. In 1789 many rose against landlords, and they gained when feudal dues were abolished. Some still had to pay to be freed from them or had little land.
Paris workers, craftsmen and shopkeepers. They joined marches and took part in local politics, and they pressed for lower bread prices and harsh measures against enemies.
women marched to Versailles, joined clubs and petitioned for their rights. They did not win the vote or the right to hold office.
Ordinary people shaped events and were changed by them, but the gains were uneven. Many hopes for a fairer life were not met.
draft.remember: Ordinary people helped drive the revolution, but some groups gained more than others.

a.q: Which statement best describes how ordinary people were affected by the revolution?
opts: They took part in events, but their gains differed by group
All groups gained equal rights and power
They played no part, as politicians made every decision
They gained nothing, because feudal dues stayed in place
a.why: Peasants, sans-culottes and women all took part, but peasants gained from the end of feudal dues while women did not win political rights. So gains were uneven rather than equal.
a.clue: Compare what peasants and women won.

b.q: In 1793 Claudine, a Parisian woman, joins a club and petitions for women's rights, but cannot vote. What does her case show?
opts: Women took part but did not gain equal political rights
Women held the same political rights as men by 1793
Women stayed away from politics in the revolution
Women gained more from the revolution than peasants did
b.why: Claudine acted politically, yet she could not vote, so participation did not bring equal rights. The claim that women had the same rights as men is wrong because she was excluded from voting.
b.clue: Notice both what she did and what she could not do.

a.best: They took part in events, but their gains differed by group

b.best: Women took part but did not gain equal political rights
